Is the Aurelian Basin still warming? (invented explainer)

Every place, number and finding on this page is invented for this repository's tests. It imitates the boilerplate shapes of an agency explainer page — breadcrumbs, menus, a social-follow block, related-content teasers, an archive banner — around substantive invented content.

How do we know the basin is warming?

Basin-mean surface temperature has risen by 1.9 °C since the 1861–1880 baseline. It is very likely that warming will continue through mid-century under every pathway assessed for the basin.

Researchers follow NASA-style calibration practices when homogenising the station record, so the observed trend is robust to instrument moves and re-sitings.

  • Terrace glaciers lost 14% of their mapped area between 1990 and 2024, the fastest loss in the invented record.
  • Southern-terrace rainfall declined from 640 mm to 550 mm per year over the same period.

Data are updated quarterly by the observatory.

Weren't there warnings of basin cooling years ago?

A handful of 1970s articles speculated about a coming basin cooling, but the assessed literature of that decade already leaned toward warming, and the observations gathered since have settled the question.

Related warming feedbacks

Loss of terrace snow lowers the basin's albedo, which amplifies the warming that caused the loss — an assessed feedback carried in every basin projection.
